candidate.title: RAD / PE RAD-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned poster row is jointly labeled RAD / PE RAD-Seq under DNA Rearrangements and Markers. It depicts a shared genomic-DNA library-preparation route ending at amplified DNA: restriction digestion, barcoded-adapter addition, combined shearing and size selection, P2-adapter addition, and amplification. RAD and PE RAD-Seq are the two targets; RAD-PE is a catalogue-supported alias for PE RAD-Seq. The independently labeled lower ddRADseq row has its own Genome-to-DNA route and no connecting branch; it is adjacent poster context, not an alternative within the assigned row. The partially visible Bisulfite conversion panel at the right is also outside scope. This resolves the previous candidate scope expansion by removing the dd_ graph, its method scope and its implementation Unknown; paper:26279345 remains unassigned background. Sequencing and paired-end assembly explain potential readout but are not depicted operations. Shared schematic preparation does not establish identical complete implementations or interchangeability of the named methods.

operations.label: Restriction digestion
operations.description: Cut genomic DNA at restriction sites, converting intact genomic substrate into restriction fragments. The separate Restriction sites drawing annotates the substrate; it is not a second transformation.

operations.information_effect: Defines genomic anchor positions for the subsequently retained restriction-associated fragments.

operations.label: Shear and size select
operations.description: Fragment the adapter-bearing DNA by shearing and retain a selected size range. The displayed products are shorter DNA fragments retaining one original barcoded restriction-site end and exposing a distal end for P2 attachment. The two actions remain one combined depicted operation.
operations.mechanism: Random shearing followed by size selection, supported by the primary RAD description.
operations.information_effect: Retains restriction-site-proximal genomic sequence and its barcode while variable distal cuts reduce fragment length; size selection restricts which molecules enter the displayed library route.

operations.label: Add P2 adapter
operations.description: Attach a second adapter at the distal end of the displayed first-adapter-bearing fragments; the resulting DNA carries both adapter interfaces.
operations.mechanism: Paper-supported interpretation: Baird identifies P2 as a divergent Y adapter. Reverse-primer binding requires complementary sequence to be filled during the first P1-initiated extension in amplification; this explains subsequent enrichment of molecules that carry P1.
operations.information_effect: Adds the second library interface while retaining the genomic insert and the existing barcode-bearing end.

operations.label: Amplify
operations.description: Amplify adapter-bearing restriction-associated DNA to produce the terminal DNA library. The number of cartoon lines is illustrative, not a measured yield.
operations.mechanism: PCR enriches P1-bearing RAD tags using the P1/P2 adapter architecture described in Baird et al.; the endpoint simplification does not imply that adapters are removed.
operations.information_effect: Increases copies of the represented restriction-site-adjacent loci while retaining barcode association. Sequencing can reveal nearby SNPs for genotyping; this reduced representation does not measure every genomic base. Illumina notes coverage gaps and loss of shared loci with restriction-site polymorphism.

checks.rationale: The inspected candidate covers both assigned upper-row targets and all five depicted transformations with six material states and ten consistent consumption/production edges. Every operation is single-input/single-output; the image shows one preparation route shared by the two labels, not two independently processed branches collapsed into a joint operation. The separately labeled lower ddRADseq route and partial bisulfite panel are neighboring context, as the card scope also specifies. Each retained adapter-bearing material follows the correct outgoing route, and no pooling, compartment, attachment, end-group, sequencing, or assembly transformation is invented. Barcode association, reduced representation, selection limits, and abstract-versus-full-text support are preserved. Relevant Baird full text agrees with the upper route, so no consequential source correction or blocking architectural unknown is required. All 14 paper associations and both method scopes were checked individually below.
